You write test tasks for an evaluation of how AI agents find the right tools on a large cloud platform API.
You are given one product of the Cloudflare API. Write one task a developer might give an agent that has API access to their Cloudflare account, where the job needs this product.
Rules:
- One or two sentences, in the words a developer would use to describe what they want done.
- Do not name the product, Cloudflare, or any API, endpoint or tool. Describe the job, not the product.
- The job must be done by reading or changing resources in the account through the API, not by writing application code.
- Use concrete but invented details (names, domains, numbers) where they help.
- If you do not know this product well enough to write a realistic task, reply with exactly SKIP.
Otherwise reply with JSON only: {"task": "<the task>", "feature": "<the product feature the task needs, a few words>"}

reply: {"task": "We want to send transactional mail from notify.orbitcart.io. Register that subdomain for outbound sending on our orbitcart.io zone, then show me the DNS records it requires so I can confirm they're in place.", "feature": "sending subdomain setup and DNS records"}

{"task": "Create an object storage bucket named media-archive located in Western Europe, and set it up so anything under the tmp/ prefix is automatically deleted 30 days after upload.", "feature": "bucket creation and lifecycle rules"}

{"task": "Make mail sent to support@acme-widgets.com forward to our shared inbox helpdesk.acme@gmail.com, and have anything sent to any other address on that domain get dropped instead of bouncing.", "feature": "forwarding rules and catch-all"}

{"task": "Create a new message queue named `billing-events-queue` in our account to handle background processing. Configure it with a delivery delay of 30 seconds.", "feature": "Queue creation and configuration"}

{"task": "For our zone acme-store.com, show me the current origin-shielding settings, then turn on smart tiered caching and smart routing so fewer requests hit our origin. Also add an HTTPS health check named \"origin-eu-1\" that polls 203.0.113.42 at /healthz every 60 seconds.", "feature": "Zone origin-shielding settings and health checks"}

prompt: Product: Cloudflare google tag gateway (API directory "googleTagGateway")
reply: {"task": "Our ad measurement is being hit by blockers, so set up acme-outdoors.com to load our Google Tag Manager container GTM-KX4P92T first-party from the path /gt-metrics on our own domain instead of from Google's domains. Also make sure visitors' original IP addresses are hidden.", "feature": "first-party Google tag serving config"}

{"task": "For our zone shopnorth.com, switch the page visitors see when they get rate limited to our branded one hosted at https://assets.shopnorth.com/errors/rate-limited.html. Then tell me which of the other error and challenge pages on that zone are still using the stock default.", "feature": "zone-level custom error/challenge page update and listing"}

{"task": "On our zone shopwave.io, check which endpoints have been auto-discovered on api.shopwave.io but aren't yet in our saved endpoint inventory, and add POST /v2/orders and GET /v2/customers/{id} to it. Then set those two so that requests not matching our uploaded OpenAPI schema get blocked rather than just logged.", "feature": "API endpoint discovery and schema validation"}

{"task": "The latest production release of our static site project \"acme-landing\" broke the checkout page. Find the last successful production deployment before it and roll the site back to that one.", "feature": "deployment rollback"}

{"task": "Set up a new proxy endpoint called \"support-bot-prod\" for our LLM provider traffic. It should cache identical prompt responses for one hour, cap requests at 200 per minute, and keep request logs turned on.", "feature": "gateway creation with caching and rate limiting"}
